title: When the Gravity Breaks Anew
premise: Zephyrine Quintana, a clone of the murdered astrogator Vela Quintana, hauls freight along the Silent Corridor, the shipping route between two worlds that severed contact after Vela's death. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, Zephyrine discovers the event was a message encoded in spacetime by Vela herself before dying—a warning that the relay at the edge of dead space is being used to falsify the official record of her murder. Pursued by the Meridian Combine's enforcers and haunted by inherited memories that may not be entirely copies, Zephyrine races a rival ship to the relay. At the relay, Zephyrine must choose between broadcasting the truth, which will shatter the fragile peace keeping the two worlds from war, or staying loyal to the crew who raised them. They broadcast it, and the final chapter finds Zephyrine, stripped of their route and their name's protection, opening the first legal trade run between the reconciled worlds—carrying Vela's original memory core as cargo, finally at rest.
about_author: Orsen Sterling is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio officer who spent eleven years running cargo between island ports before turning to fiction. Their work is known for claustrophobic shipboard tension and stories about people who inherit debts they never chose.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Mid-run between the worlds of Calla and Vesper, gravity fails for exactly nine seconds; cargo drifts, Zephyrine nearly dies in the hold, and every ship in the system broadcasts the same confused panic. The emotional beat is disorientation—the first crack in a life built on routine and deliberate invisibility.

chapters.title: The Route No One Speaks Of
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with flashbacks in Vela's voice from inherited memory. Establishes the Silent Corridor: two worlds that stopped speaking after Vela Quintana's unsolved murder, and Zephyrine's precarious livelihood running their border. Beat: loneliness and the weight of a name that opens doors and closes others.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Scars
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A med-exam reveals anomalies in the clone's memory imprint—recalled sensations Vela never logged, including the moment of her death. Zephyrine's handler, Ivo Reyes, urges them to report nothing. Beat: creeping dread that the copy is contaminated, or worse, that it's a message.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Auditing cargo records to explain the flicker, Zephyrine finds nine seconds of telemetry missing from every ship's log—erased, not lost. A Meridian Combine inspector boards and asks questions about Vela's last run. Beat: paranoia; someone is curating the past.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Airlock
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Zephyrine and Sable Oduya, captain of the rival courier Bright Meridian. Sable delivers a warning from the Combine: stand down or be decommissioned. Zephyrine recognizes her from Vela's memories—an old friend, now an enemy. Beat: betrayal across a generation.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Deep in the memory archive, Zephyrine isolates Vela's final hours: she discovered the edge-relay was rewriting official records and hid a proof-key inside the gravity lattice itself. The nine-second flicker was the key surfacing. Beat: revelation—the flicker was a message, and Zephyrine is its only reader.

chapters.title: Crew of Small Loyalties
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating POV among Zephyrine's three crewmates: engineer Dov, navigator Ash, and cook Marisol. Each privately weighs whether Zephyrine's obsession will get them killed. Beat: loyalty tested in the galley and the engine room; the crew chooses to stay, for now.

chapters.title: The Combine's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sable Oduya's POV. Inside the Meridian Combine, Sable learns the flicker wasn't an accident and that Director Hale wants Zephyrine's ship quietly destroyed before the relay can be reached. Sable hesitates. Beat: the antagonist's conscience begins to fracture.

chapters.title: Departure Without Clearance
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The crew votes to run for the edge relay, off-manifest and off-grid, using Vela's hidden astrogation notes. Dov refuses and disembarks. Beat: the cost of commitment—leaving a friend on the dock, knowing the route back may not exist.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Weeks in dead space; the ship's systems degrade, and Zephyrine's inherited memories intensify, bleeding into waking hours until they answer to Vela's name. Beat: identity erosion—the terror that the clone is becoming the original, or being consumed by her.

chapters.title: Intercept at Cinder Shoals
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The Bright Meridian corners them in an asteroid shoal. Instead of attacking, Sable boards and reveals Hale falsified Vela's murder investigation—and that Sable's silence bought her crew's lives. Beat: uneasy alliance; enemy and heir share the same grief.

chapters.title: Proof in the Lattice
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Sable, joint POV. Decoding Vela's proof-key, they learn the relay doesn't just falsify records—it's being used to fabricate an incident that will justify Calla striking Vesper first. Beat: stakes escalate from personal truth to systemic war.

chapters.title: The Message They Sent Twice
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A second nine-second flicker hits—Vela's dead-man switch, warning that the relay now knows someone is coming. Marisol confronts Zephyrine about whether they're following Vela's plan or Vela's ghost. Beat: the theme of loyalty vs. truth made intimate and domestic.

chapters.title: What Ivo Knew
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A delayed transmission from Ivo Reyes reveals he was Vela's handler too—and that he approved the clone program specifically to preserve the memory key, making Zephyrine's entire existence a delivery mechanism. Beat: fury and vertigo; even their creation was someone else's plan.

chapters.title: Running the Broken Clock
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. The race tightens: the Combine's warships burn for the relay, and the fabricated incident is scheduled to trigger in six days. The ship takes damage threading an unmapped current. Beat: desperation and competence under pressure; the crew becomes a single organism.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. They arrive to find the relay station crewed, armed, and expecting them—Hale himself aboard. Sable's cover holds just long enough to get them inside. Beat: cold dread in a place that hums with stolen history; the truth is one room away.

chapters.title: Archive of a Murder
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In the relay's sealed archive, Zephyrine finds the original records of Vela's death—including the name of her killer: Director Hale's predecessor, now a revered statesman whose exposure could still ignite the war Vela died preventing. Beat: truth revealed as a double-edged inheritance.

chapters.title: Hale's Bargain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Zephyrine and Hale. Hale offers Zephyrine everything—Vela's estate, the route, legitimacy—in exchange for silence. He argues the lie is the only wall holding back war. Beat: the central choice made flesh; loyalty to the dead versus loyalty to the living.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The crew seizes the relay's transmitter while Sable holds off Combine marines; Zephyrine must physically merge with the memory core to authenticate Vela's key, risking their own mind in the process. They broadcast everything. Beat: climax—sacrifice, clarity, and the irreversible act.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a True Sentence
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The broadcast lands: Calla and Vesper halt on the brink, Hale is arrested, and the old killer's legacy burns. Sable testifies, trading her freedom for her crew's. Beat: reckoning—truth costs what loyalty cost, and pays in the same coin.

chapters.title: Two Voices in One Hold
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Recovering from the merge, Zephyrine negotiates with the residue of Vela's memories—not erasing them, but making peace: two lives sharing one body by consent. Beat: quiet, tender resolution of the identity thread; inheritance accepted rather than endured.

chapters.title: First Run, New Gravity
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Months later, Zephyrine pilots the first legal ship between Calla and Vesper, carrying Vela's memory core as registered cargo to a public archive. Gravity holds steady. Beat: hope earned—the route between worlds is open, and the dead are finally allowed to rest.
